# evidtrail

> AI provenance for git: declared at commit time, checked in CI, traceable to the agent session. Honest about what git cannot prove.

evidtrail (formerly AIDA Metrics) is an open-source CLI and GitHub Action. It makes every commit state how it was produced, and checks that it did. A git hook writes the autonomy level (`AI-Mode:`) and the tool (`Assisted-by:`, the convention of the Linux kernel, Fedora and LLVM) at commit time, and, if the person opts in, the agent session the commit came from (`AI-Session:`). `evidtrail verify` fails a pull request whose commits state nothing, like a DCO check for `Signed-off-by`. The report opens with provenance: per commit, the autonomy level (`none`, `autocomplete`, `assisted`, `agent`, or `unknown`) and how that is known (`declared`, `inferred`, or no evidence). Repository change signals (fixed-horizon rapid retouch, reverts, hotfixes and their trend) follow as an appendix.

## What evidtrail is not

evidtrail does not infer productivity, defects, deployment, causality, capitalization, or developer performance from git history. It does not measure the quality of AI-written code: mistakes an agent makes and fixes inside its session never reach git, and churn says little about accuracy. It does not estimate the value of software.

## How evidence is produced

- A `prepare-commit-msg` hook, installed once per clone (or via a `package.json` `prepare` script), detects agent sessions from their environment and stamps `AI-Mode:` and `Assisted-by:` trailers. This needs no per-commit discipline.
- `Assisted-by:` written by people is read as a declaration of AI involvement; the autonomy level stays `unknown` unless `AI-Mode:` states it.
- With `git config evidtrail.recordSession true`, AI commits also carry `AI-Session: <agent>/<id>`. `evidtrail trail <commit>` finds the transcript locally and never opens it.
- Tool co-author trailers (for example `Co-Authored-By: Claude`) are read as inferred evidence.
- A commit with no signal stays `unknown`. It is never assumed to be human.
- A configured `defaultMode` acts only at commit time, when the hook stamps it. Analysis applies it to nothing: commits with no evidence stay `unknown`, and coverage never rises.
- There is no AI-vs-human comparison of change signals (removed in 2.0): in most repositories one side is empty, and where both exist the gap reflects the work each group did more than the code.

## Honesty mechanisms worth knowing

- Trends compare only mature periods: every period is judged on the same fixed horizon, and a period is comparable only after it has been over for that horizon. Otherwise every report would find retouch rising.
- Scope is explicit: default-branch ancestry by default; all refs and PR change sets are opt-in and labelled.
- Analysis is deterministic from a collected snapshot; output schemas are versioned and readers refuse incompatible inputs.
- Collection, analysis and reporting are local. Only `fetch-prs` and `comment` use the network, both opt-in.

## Commands

- `evidtrail init` — set up config, commit hook, prepare script, CI workflow (additive)
- `evidtrail doctor` — preflight: clone depth, partial clone, config, hook, CI wiring
- `evidtrail` — collect → analyze → report
- `evidtrail verify` — fail when commits in scope do not state their provenance (exit 1), DCO-style
- `evidtrail trail <commit>` — follow a commit to what it states and to its agent session
- `evidtrail collect`, `evidtrail analyze`, `evidtrail report`, `evidtrail blame`, `evidtrail fetch-prs`, `evidtrail comment`, `evidtrail install-hooks`
